# Nostrord - Full Context

> Nostrord is a free, open-source NIP-29 client for decentralized group chat on Nostr. Built with Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) and Compose, it brings a Discord-style experience to a censorship-resistant protocol, with relay-enforced moderation, cryptographic identity, and no sign-up required.

## What is Nostrord?

Nostrord is a cross-platform group messaging application built on top of Nostr (Notes and Other Stuff Transmitted by Relays) and implements NIP-29, the Nostr Improvement Proposal that defines relay-based groups.

Unlike centralized platforms like Discord, Telegram, or Slack where a company controls the servers and can ban users, delete communities, or shut down, Nostrord groups live on public Nostr relays that anyone can run. Membership, moderation, and access control are enforced by the relay hosting the group, and users can switch relays without losing their identity.

## What is NIP-29?

NIP-29 is the Nostr specification for relay-based groups. It defines:

- Group creation and metadata (name, description, picture)
- Member management (add, remove, list)
- Admin roles and permissions (promote, demote, moderate)
- Message posting and threading
- Group discovery and invites
- Relay-side authorization (the relay decides who can post)

This differs from IRC-style channels because groups have persistent state, moderation tools, and cryptographic identity. It differs from Matrix or federated chat because there is no federation protocol - each group lives on a single relay.

Current release: v2.10.1

## Key Features

### Core Messaging

- Real-time chat via WebSocket subscriptions to Nostr relays
- Replies inside chat (kind:9 carrying a `q` tag, the NIP-C7 convention; NIP-10 `e`-marker replies are only tolerated on read)
- Quote events, @mentions (NIP-27), and rich text rendering
- Inline image, video, and audio playback, plus YouTube link cards and an image viewer with zoom and pan
- Emoji reactions with a categorized Unicode picker and recent-emoji memory. Custom emoji (NIP-30) arriving from other clients are rendered inline, but the picker does not offer custom emoji to send
- Image, video, and audio uploads to Blossom servers (multi-server with mirroring) or a NIP-96 host, selectable in Settings, with `imeta` media tags (NIP-92) for dimensions, mime, hash, and size
- Message deletion (by author or admin) per NIP-09
- Threads: forum-style discussions built on NIP-22 comments (kind:1111) over a NIP-29 forum root, with reactions, mentions and a split view on desktop

### Notifications and Unread

- Per-group unread state across sessions, tracked by `UnreadManager`
- Focus-aware muting: the conversation you are actively reading does not generate notifications
- On web: browser notifications via the Notification API and tab-title badges (e.g. `(3) Nostrord`)
- On native (Android, iOS, Desktop JVM): notifications are no-op stubs; unread tracking still works in-app. There is no FCM/APNs push and no system notification tray integration

### Group Management and Moderation

- Group creation flow with metadata (name, description, picture)
- Invite codes for controlled access to private groups
- Join requests review (approve or reject incoming members)
- Edit group metadata (name, description, picture, type)
- Add or remove members; promote and demote admins
- Per-member permissions (post, moderate, invite)
- Relay-enforced membership (the relay rejects unauthorized events)
- Message removal by admins
- Channels: a single-level hierarchy of NIP-29 groups (kind:39000 `parent`/`child` tags, not part of the NIP-29 spec) rendered as a sidebar tree, with admin-gated channel creation, drag-and-drop ordering and a Manage > Hierarchy tab. Not behind an app feature flag, but the whole UI is hidden unless the relay advertises `nip29.subgroups` in its NIP-11 document, which most public NIP-29 relays do not.

### Identity and Signing

- Nostr keypair identity (no email, phone, or username)
- NIP-07 browser extension support for web signing
- NIP-46 remote signer (bunker) for hardware-like separation of keys
- NIP-55 external signer on Android (Amber or any compatible signer app)
- NIP-49 password-protected private keys (ncryptsec) for import and export
- Login with Google (Pomegranate), built on the promenade FROST threshold signer: the Nostr key is split into shards held by independent operators and the client signs over plain NIP-46 through a coordinator, so no single party, Nostrord included, holds the whole key. The user can export the nsec at any time. Available on web, Android and desktop; iOS in progress
- Multiple accounts with one-tap switching, each with its own session and storage
- NIP-19 bech32 encoding (npub, nsec, note, nevent, naddr)
- NIP-42 relay authentication

### Privacy

- Encrypted direct messages via NIP-17 gift wrap (kind:14 chat, kind:15 files) sealed with NIP-44 and wrapped with NIP-59, so relays see neither content nor the conversation graph
- User-configurable DM relays (kind:10050)
- NIP-04 encrypted direct messages kept only for compatibility with older clients
- User mute lists (NIP-51), synced across devices as self-encrypted app data (NIP-78)
- No analytics, no telemetry
- No account server, no data harvesting

### Payments

- Lightning zaps (NIP-57) on any message and on profiles
- `lud16`/`lud06` resolved through LNURL-pay, zap request (kind 9734) signed by the user, invoice paid in the user's own wallet via QR code, `lightning:` URI or copy, and confirmed by watching for the zap receipt (kind 9735)
- No custodial wallet, no in-app balance, no platform fee

### Live Audio and Video Spaces

- Live audio and video rooms inside a NIP-29 group. Media runs on a LiveKit SFU that the relay operator deploys alongside the relay, with tokens minted at `/.well-known/nip29/livekit/<group-id>`, so this is not the Nostr relay carrying the media
- Presence is a `livekit` tag on kind:39000, enabled by an admin via kind:9002; the live roster is kind:39004, a convention rather than part of NIP-29
- Clients on web, Android and desktop, with a live-space bar for joining an ongoing room. The room is created lazily by the first participant
- Only a few relays run the companion today, for example pyramid.fiatjaf.com

### Discovery

- Discover tab built from the people you follow (NIP-02) and their public group lists (kind:10009), ranked by how many of your contacts are members
- Recommended tab seeded from a curated group list
- Light and dark themes, following the system setting or a manual choice

### Multi-Platform

- Web: runs in any modern browser as a DOM-based app (live at https://web.nostrord.com/)
- Android: native Kotlin app via Compose Multiplatform (APK available on GitHub Releases)
- Windows: native desktop app via Compose Multiplatform (MSI installer available on GitHub Releases)
- macOS: native desktop app via Compose Multiplatform (DMG for Apple Silicon available on GitHub Releases)
- Linux: native desktop app via Compose Multiplatform (.deb and .rpm on GitHub Releases, Arch package on the AUR as `nostrord-bin`)
- iOS: Compose Multiplatform UI (in development)

Pre-built binaries for Android, Windows, macOS and Linux are published on GitHub Releases. The dynamic downloads page at https://nostrord.com/download/ always serves the latest release for the visitor's detected platform.

## How It Works

1. The user opens Nostrord on any platform
2. The user authenticates with a Nostr keypair (existing or generated) or connects via NIP-07 (browser extension) or NIP-46 (remote signer)
3. The user connects to one or more NIP-29-compatible relays (e.g., groups.0xchat.com)
4. The user can create a new group, browse public groups, or accept an invite
5. When sending a message, the client constructs a Nostr event, signs it with the private key, and publishes it to the group's relay
6. The relay validates membership and permissions, then broadcasts to all subscribed members
7. Other clients receive the event in real time and render it in the group chat

## Architecture

Nostrord uses Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) with Compose Multiplatform for UI, sharing the majority of code across all target platforms.

### Module Map

- `composeApp/commonMain`: shared business logic, view models, NIP implementations
- `composeApp/uiComposeMain`: shared Compose UI for Android, desktop and iOS
- `composeApp/androidMain`: Android-specific storage and crypto
- `composeApp/jvmMain`: JVM Desktop crypto (secp256k1-kmp), JVM Preferences
- `composeApp/jsMain`: NIP-07 window.nostr, JS Ktor client, DOM-based web UI (the build live at web.nostrord.com)

### Core Components

- `NostrRepository`: public facade for group/message operations
- `SessionManager`: authentication and NIP-42 handling
- `AuthManager`: low-level key and signer management
- `GroupManager`: NIP-29 group logic, including the channel hierarchy and threads
- `DmManager`: NIP-17 gift-wrapped direct messages
- `ZapManager`: NIP-57 zap requests, invoices and receipts
- `ConnectionManager`: WebSocket lifecycle across relays
- `OutboxManager` and `RelayListManager`: NIP-65 outbox model and relay list resolution
- `UnreadManager`: per-group unread tracking with focus-aware suppression
- `NotificationService`: platform abstraction over browser Notification API (web) and no-op stubs (native)
- `EventDeduplicator`: dedup events across multiple relays
- `AppModule`: dependency injection entry point

### Key Dependencies

- Ktor 3.0 for WebSocket and HTTP
- secp256k1-kmp 0.14 for elliptic curve cryptography (Android + JVM)
- BouncyCastle 1.78 for auxiliary crypto
- kotlinx.serialization for JSON parsing
- Coil 3.x for image loading
- EncryptedSharedPreferences for Android key storage

## Supported NIPs

| NIP | Description | Status |
|-----|-------------|--------|
| NIP-01 | Basic protocol (events, subscriptions) | Implemented |
| NIP-02 | Follow list | Implemented |
| NIP-04 | Encrypted direct messages | Legacy, compatibility only |
| NIP-05 | DNS-based identifiers | Displayed, not verified |
| NIP-07 | Browser signer extension | Implemented (web) |
| NIP-09 | Event deletion | Implemented |
| NIP-11 | Relay information document | Implemented |
| NIP-17 | Private direct messages | Implemented |
| NIP-19 | bech32 entities | Implemented |
| NIP-22 | Comments (kind:1111) | Implemented (threads) |
| NIP-25 | Reactions | Implemented |
| NIP-27 | Text note references and mentions | Implemented |
| NIP-29 | Relay-based groups | Core focus |
| NIP-30 | Custom emoji | Implemented |
| NIP-42 | Relay authentication | Implemented |
| NIP-44 | Versioned encryption | Implemented |
| NIP-46 | Remote signer (bunker) | Implemented |
| NIP-49 | Private key encryption (ncryptsec) | Implemented |
| NIP-51 | Lists (mute list) | Implemented |
| NIP-55 | Android signer application (Amber and compatible) | Implemented (Android) |
| NIP-56 | Reporting | Implemented |
| NIP-57 | Lightning zaps | Implemented (send and receive) |
| NIP-59 | Gift wrap | Implemented |
| NIP-65 | Relay list metadata | Implemented |
| NIP-92 | Media attachments (imeta tags) | Implemented |
| NIP-78 | Application-specific data | Implemented |
| NIP-84 | Highlights | Implemented |
| NIP-96 | HTTP file storage | Implemented |
| NIP-98 | HTTP authentication | Implemented |

## Why Nostrord?

### vs Centralized Platforms (Discord, Telegram)

- No company can ban you, delete your community, or shut down
- Your identity is a cryptographic key, portable across all Nostr apps
- Anyone can run a relay to host a group
- Moderation is transparent and user-controlled
- No phone number, email, or personal data required

### vs Federated Platforms (Matrix, Mastodon)

- Simpler protocol (no federation complexity)
- Lightweight clients (no homeserver required)
- Faster message delivery (direct WebSocket to relay)
- Unified identity across all apps (not scoped to a server)

### vs Other Nostr Clients

- Purpose-built for NIP-29 groups, not general Nostr
- Channels, threads, encrypted DMs, zaps and live audio and video spaces in one client
- Kotlin Multiplatform (true native, not Electron)
- Compose UI on the native apps, a React DOM UI on the web, both on the same shared Kotlin core
- Open source under the Unlicense (public domain)

## Platform Support

- Web: https://web.nostrord.com/ (live beta)
- Android: native APK on GitHub Releases (Google Play listing planned)
- Windows: MSI installer on GitHub Releases (x64)
- macOS: DMG on GitHub Releases (Apple Silicon; Intel build planned)
- Linux: .deb and .rpm packages on GitHub Releases plus `nostrord-bin` on the AUR (x64; AppImage and other distros planned)
- iOS: native via Compose Multiplatform (in development)

Downloads hub: https://nostrord.com/download/ (auto-detects platform, always serves latest release)
Releases: https://github.com/nostrord/nostrord/releases

## Funding

Nostrord has been awarded a grant by OpenSats in their sixteenth wave of Nostr grants (April 2026). This funding enables focused development toward a stable v1 release.

Announcement: https://opensats.org/blog/sixteenth-wave-of-nostr-grants
